summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, post-transplant chronic graft-versus-host disease, BOOP, cardiomyopathy, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for a recurrent left-sided perianal abscess with persistent pain, dehydration, and symptomatic hypotension. He underwent incision and drainage with placement of a Malecot drain, which was later downsized. He was treated with intravenous fluids, vancomycin, and piperacillin-tazobactam, later narrowed to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. His acute kidney injury from dehydration improved with rehydration, and his metabolic acidosis resolved. His home heart failure medications were held initially due to hypotension and restarted sequentially. He was discharged home with the drain in place, on a plan for antibiotic continuation, drain care, and follow-up. Oxygen therapy was adjusted to 1 liter continuously and 3 liters with exertion due to borderline hypoxemia.
